findings.title: The checker is entirely STREAM-BLIND and nothing in the tree notices -- the per-stream keying that is the SUBJECT of I2 is the one property with no fixture
findings.failure_scenario: MEASURED, one mutation, applied alone to the staged bytes: replace every `run.key()` in the checker with a single constant key -- `nextOffset.getOrDefault(new RunKey(new UUID(0,0), 0), 0L)` at :117, `nextOffset.put(new RunKey(new UUID(0,0), 0), ...)` at :136, `inherited.merge(new RunKey(new UUID(0,0), 0), ...)` at :254. Result: `./gradlew :sequencer:test` 182 tests, 0 failing, BUILD SUCCESSFUL. The weaker version the test-reviewer reported (collapse only the fold's partition, `new RunKey(run.key().indexId(), 0)`) also survives 182/0. CAUSE: `InvariantFixtures.counts(n)` and `InvariantFixtures.delta(...)` both hard-code `new RunKey(A, 0)`, so all 19 invariant fixtures are one index and one partition and the map may as well be a scalar. CONCRETE FAILURE: with two streams the running mark becomes the MAX over all streams, so a genuine `gap` in stream S1 (S1 mark 3, jumps to 9) is compared against a global mark of 12 contributed by S2 and is reported as I2 -- data corruption where there is only a hole. That is verbatim the confusion the comment at Invariants.java:118-126 says 'buries the real thing', it is the distinction M4.16's whole diagnosis turns on ('a REWIND, not a gap'), and M4.13 pins EXACT counts and kinds. WHY MINOR AND NOT MAJOR, stated so it can be argued rather than trusted: because `Math.max`/`Math::max` makes the collapsed mark never LOWER than any stream's true mark, every genuine I2 rewind is still caught -- the error is in the false-positive and wrong-KIND direction, loud rather than silent, and it manifests the instant any fixture or sweep uses a second stream. It is also T1 test-only code over MemoryBinStore. But it deserves a ROW rather than a commit-body line, on the same standard that produced M4.23 and M4.25: this class's entire five-round history is about arms that cannot go false, the class advertises I2 -- whose statement is per-stream -- and the whole product exists to bundle MANY indices and partitions, so a checker that cannot tell two streams apart is not yet checking I2 for the system it will be pointed at. Remedy is one fixture, cheaper than either fixture this round added: a chain with `RunKey(A, 0)` and `RunKey(A, 1)` where the second resumes correctly at its OWN mark while the first sits higher, asserted `isEmpty()` -- which the collapsed mutant reports as I2.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a two-stream fixture (a second RunKey(A, 1) via an overload of `counts`/`delta`) asserting that each stream's mark is tracked independently, or record it on a new row alongside M4.23/M4.25 and say in the commit body that the per-stream keying ships unpinned.

findings.title: `readChain`'s pagination loop is unfalsifiable, and this is the only SILENT survivor -- a chain over 1000 entries reports CLEAN for everything past entry 1000
findings.failure_scenario: MEASURED, one mutation: delete `if (page.nextStartAfter().isEmpty()) { return out; } after = page.nextStartAfter().get();` and return after the first page. Result 182 tests, 0 failing. Consequence, and it is a false NEGATIVE rather than a false positive: `checkChain` on a chain of 1001 entries examines the first 1000, reports no violation for a reassignment at entry 1001, and the caller cannot tell that from clean -- which is precisely 'a checker that never fails is worse than no checker' (InvariantsTest.java:21) occurring in the checker. It also silently truncates the seal scan and the inheritance fold, so a barrier beyond entry 1000 is invisible and a successor inherits a fenced writer's offsets. I AGREE WITH THE TEST REVIEWER THAT THIS IS MINOR, and the reason is a length bound rather than the remedy's price: `SmallPageStore`'s own javadoc says the alternative is a 1100-object fixture, and no chain the harness builds comes near it -- M4.16 records 8 commits across 39 burned epochs, and M4.13's stated budget is <60s for 1,000 seeds, so nothing in the foreseeable sweep reaches 1000 entries in ONE chain. THE PRECEDENT ARGUMENT DOES CUT THE OTHER WAY AND SHOULD BE ON THE RECORD: `SmallPageStore` exists in this exact package because `CommitLog.recover` had this same blind spot (its javadoc: 'Measured -- the mutation survived the whole sequencer suite'), it is applied at three call sites in CommitLogSealTest and CommitLogSealWriteTest, and this commit -- whose five rounds have been about nothing but unfalsified arms -- reintroduced the blind spot one class over. So it is the closest of the four survivors to major, and the remedy is one measured line rather than any prose: I applied `Invariants.checkChain(new SmallPageStore(store, 2), PREFIX, 1)` at InvariantsTest.java:59 together with the truncation mutation and `anEntryBEYONDASealIsReportedAsI5` fails, then reverted both. Zero new fixtures, zero new comment.
findings.suggested_fix: Wrap the store in `new SmallPageStore(store, 2)` at one existing `checkChain` call site whose chain has more than two entries (InvariantsTest.java:59 works, verified), or take the row.

findings.title: A row marked **done** still states three defects in the PRESENT TENSE that this same commit removed
findings.failure_scenario: The row retains verbatim '⚠️ Also: the I2 rewind boundary IS unpinned by one record, `crossEpochOffsetsChecked()` IS a hard-coded true with an assertion around it, and two fixtures BUILD a `LeaseManager` on `Clock.systemUTC()` in the package that now owns `SimulatedClock`' and then, a clause later, says each was fixed -- the one-record boundary by `anOverlapOfEXACTLYONERecord`, the flag by deletion ('`crossEpochOffsetsChecked()` IS DELETED rather than fixed'), the clock by `InvariantFixtures.FIXED_CLOCK`. All three fixes are real and I verified them in the staged bytes: `grep -c crossEpochOffsetsChecked` over the whole tree is 0 outside this row's own prose, and the one-record fixture is falsifiable (`< from` -> `< from - 1` is the mutation it names). CONCRETE CONSEQUENCE: `milestone-review` and any future reader take these rows as the record of what happened, and this closed row tells them the shipped checker contains a hard-coded `return true` -- the exact defect it was closed for removing. This is the 'row describes a commit other than itself' mechanism that the M4.12 row two lines above carries three separate banners about, and that R4-2 was a smaller instance of. It costs one word each ('WAS', 'WAS', 'BUILT') or the whole clause deleted, since the later clause already says it.
findings.suggested_fix: Put the three stale clauses in the past tense, or delete them -- the DELIVERED clause that follows already states all three outcomes.

So: InvariantsAcrossChainsTest.java:57 'with all 18 tests green' -> 19; backlog M4.25 'with all 18 invariant tests green' -> 19; InvariantsTest.java:172 'across all 181 tests' -> 182 or 178; backlog M4.23 'leaves all 180 sequencer tests green' -> 182 or 178. Each is arithmetically consistent with SOME mid-round state (182 minus the two tests this round added is 180; minus one is 181), which is exactly the problem: a reader cannot reproduce any of them, and two of them are only reachable at all in a working copy that has untracked files a fresh clone does not. I re-measured both underlying claims and BOTH survivals are real, so only the numbers are wrong: `neverOpened`'s `&& sealed.sequence() == 0` weakened to `entries.getFirst() instanceof Seal` -> 182/0 green (M4.23); `InvariantFixtures.FIXED_CLOCK` swapped to `Clock.systemUTC()` -> 182/0 green (M4.25). findings.title: Every hop of the inheritance walk reads the predecessor's chain TWICE, and M4.24 -- the row that must decide whether M4.13's budget is reachable -- does not record the doubling
findings.failure_scenario: `checkLink(store, prefix, epoch, opening, found)` at :218 does `readChain(store, prefix, opening.prevEpoch())` at :293, and line :221 immediately does `readChain(store, prefix, from)` for the same `from = opening.prevEpoch()`. Neither result is shared, so every hop costs 2 LISTs plus 2 GETs per entry of the predecessor, and the recursion at :247 pays it again at each level. Reading the code alone, the checker's per-examination request count is 2x what M4.24's row implies. CONCRETE CONSEQUENCE: M4.24 exists specifically to decide 'whether M4.13's stated budget is reachable' (<60s for 1,000 seeds) and quotes 4,999 LISTs for one examination at epoch 5000 -- a figure that comes from `firstAncestorWithDeltas`, which only runs on the `prevEpoch() < 1` branch. The doubling is on the COMMON branch and is the cheapest thing to remove (hoist one `readChain` and pass the list into `checkLink`), so a row that omits it will size the wrong problem. NOT A COST-BUDGET OBJECTION: `Invariants` is test-only, runs over `MemoryBinStore`, and no billed rate moves -- and it scales with EPOCHS, not with records, shards, partitions or indices, so non-negotiable 6 is not violated. It is a note that belongs on M4.24.
findings.suggested_fix: Add one clause to M4.24 naming the duplicate `readChain` per hop, since the obvious fix (hoist it and hand the list to `checkLink`) is also the cheapest part of that row.

findings.title: Three unused imports, one of which is a false signal about the clock
findings.failure_scenario: `import static binjava.sequencer.InvariantFixtures.FIXED_CLOCK;` (:6), `import java.io.IOException;` (:15) and `import java.util.List;` (:16) are all unused -- every test declares `throws Exception`, and `List` occurs only inside the class javadoc's `return List.of()` prose. They are the residue of the re-inlined `start` this round removed, which the class javadoc at :34-39 describes. The FIXED_CLOCK one is the one worth a word: it reads as though this class pins the clock, when in fact only the shared `start` helper does, so a reader auditing the no-wall-clock convention gets a false positive here -- and M4.25's second predicate is exactly a grep over this package for `systemUTC`. No gate catches it (`-Werror` is not on for unused imports; see M4.25's dangling-doc argument for the same shape).
findings.suggested_fix: Delete the three imports, or leave them and let M4.25's proposed compiler-warning gate pick them up.
